<description>
`wallet_keypool_topup.py` is meant to test keypool restore for four output types, one node each. But the wallet and backup paths are only set for node1, so for nodes 2-4 the test copies node1's backup over node1's running wallet and restarts the node under test on its own, never-restored wallet. The checks still pass, so only the legacy case has actually been tested since 0dcac51049.

This backs up and restores each node's own wallet, and asserts that the restored wallet rescans on startup so the test can't silently skip the restore again. Adding just that assertion on master makes the test fail at node2.

Also fixes `wallet_createwallet.py` calling `w7.walletpassphrase` where it means w8 (since c5d3787367), so the `avoid_reuse wallet` was never checked.
</description>

<commits>
215f8b828b test: restore each node's own wallet backup in wallet_keypool_topup

0dcac51049 extended this test to check keypool restore for every output
type, one node each. However, the wallet and backup paths were only
computed for node1, and only node1's wallet was backed up. For nodes
2-4, the restore step copied node1's backup over node1's wallet while
node1 was running, then restarted the node under test on its own,
never-restored wallet. The p2sh-segwit, bech32 and bech32m checks
therefore passed trivially: that wallet had derived the keys and
received the funds itself.

Back up each node's wallet with backupwallet and restore that backup
into the node under test. Assert that the restored wallet rescans on
startup, so the test fails if a node is ever restarted without its
backup again. Also update the docstring, which still described the
original two-node test.

13b2d21beb test: check w8, not w7, after creating the avoid_reuse wallet

Since c5d3787367 the avoid_reuse section of wallet_createwallet calls
w7.walletpassphrase, repeating the assertion made on w7 just before it,
so the w8 wallet it creates was never checked for encryption. Call it
on w8 to check that creating a wallet with an empty passphrase and
avoid_reuse=true leaves it unencrypted.
</commits>
